adults.title: Closer to Him, Whatever We Carry
adults.big_idea: Whatever our concerns, questions or doubts, the way to overcome them is to get closer to our Savior, Jesus Christ, whose grace is for all.
adults.objective: Learners will name what President Oaks taught us to do with a concern or doubt and choose one daily or weekly practice that will bring them closer to Jesus Christ.
prepare: Read President Oaks's talk, The Gospel of Jesus Christ Is for All, especially the paragraphs that begin “We all have present or future concerns” and “We are all a work in progress.”
Bring paper and pens, or invite learners to use a notes app.
Have learners open the talk in Gospel Library, or bring a few printed copies of those two paragraphs.
Write on the board: What does the prophet tell us to do with a concern or a doubt?
Mark Articles of Faith 1:1; 2 Nephi 26:33; 2 Nephi 29:7; and 2 Nephi 9:21.

segments.name: What we carry
steps: Begin with prayer. If you wish, sing or read one verse of Come unto Jesus.

Explain that this is the Sunday morning address of President Dallin H. Oaks, President of the Church. He said that we all have present or future concerns or struggles, and that these may include questions or doubts.
Give everyone one minute of silence to write, privately, one concern, struggle or question they are carrying now. Tell them no one will be asked to share it.
Read aloud the first key quote (T27.05). Say that today's lesson is about how to do what he describes.
questions: Why do you think the President of the Church began with the fact that all of us have concerns or struggles?

segments.name: What the prophet tells us to do
steps: Form groups of three or four. Ask each group to read the two paragraphs of the talk that begin “We all have present or future concerns” and “We are all a work in progress.”
Ask each group to list every action President Oaks gives, in his words. Allow four minutes.

Gather the lists on the board. Look for: get closer to the Savior; focus on developing faith in God and the mission of His Son; try daily, one step at a time; pray; learn from the scriptures; be patient with one another and with ourselves; build faith and strengthen humility; hold on to the first article of faith; wait upon the Lord.
Read the second key quote (T27.05) and ask the question below. Let several people answer.
questions: President Oaks said strong faith requires more than strong desire. What has daily trying looked like for you in a hard season?

segments.name: Hold on to what we know
steps: Invite someone to read or recite Articles of Faith 1:1. Then read the third key quote (T27.06).
Point out that this is a direct instruction from the President of the Church: hold on to the first article of faith even if something else is uncertain.
Give one minute of silent writing: next to the concern you wrote earlier, write what you do know about Heavenly Father, Jesus Christ and the Holy Ghost.
In pairs, share whatever you are comfortable sharing from what you wrote about what you know. The concern itself stays private.
questions: President Oaks said that waiting upon the Lord includes trusting in His timing as well as in His promises. When has that been true for you?

segments.name: Patient with one another
steps: Remind the class that President Oaks said we are all “a work in progress” and at different places on the covenant path, and that we need to be patient with one another and, occasionally, even with ourselves.
Read President Kimball's words on humility from the aligned quotes. President Oaks quoted them and said President Kimball defined humility as “teachableness.”
Discuss the questions below as a class. Keep the discussion general; no one should describe another person's struggles.
questions: How does being teachable help when a question is not answered quickly?
What does patience sound like when someone we love is at a different place on the covenant path?

segments.name: His grace is for all
steps: Ask half the class to read 2 Nephi 26:33 and the other half 2 Nephi 29:7. Each half reports who the Lord includes.
Share what President Oaks taught from these verses: “His grace is for all.” Then read the fourth key quote (T27.07), spoken to members of diminishing faith, young and old.

Read 2 Nephi 9:21 together. Explain that President Oaks taught that forgiveness through the Savior's Atonement comes as we comply with the conditions He has prescribed, including faith, repentance and baptism, and that this depends on our desires, our choices and our actions.
Read Elder Lebethoa's words from the aligned quotes as a second witness from this conference.
questions: Who might need to hear from us this week that the Savior invites all and that His grace is for all?

segments.name: Protect, strengthen and act
steps: Read the invitations aloud. Be clear about which is which: President Oaks urged us to keep the commandments and be true to our covenants; he invited all to believe the promises of the Book of Mormon; he called upon all to act on these truths and share them.
Point to his promise about the sacrament, living our covenants and, for those who have been endowed, regular attendance at the temple: “These simple practices will protect and strengthen you.”
As a check for understanding, ask one or two learners to say in one sentence what the prophet tells us to do with a concern or a doubt.
Invite everyone to write one thing from the act list they will do this week, next to the concern they wrote at the start.
Tell the class that next week you will begin by asking who is willing to share how one of these simple practices protected or strengthened them. Close with your testimony of Jesus Christ.

key_quotes.text: We all have present or future concerns or struggles we are trying to overcome. Those may include questions or doubts. Whatever they are, the way to overcome them is to get closer to our Savior, Jesus Christ.
Strong faith requires more than strong desire. It means daily trying, one step at a time, with prayer and scriptural learning.
Hold on to the first article of faith even if something else is uncertain. And while you wait, wait upon the Lord, which includes trusting in His timing as well as in His promises.
He is relentless in His loving pursuit of each of you.

scriptures.use: Read or recite it before the third key quote. Then write silently what you know about each member of the Godhead.
Half the class reads it and reports every group the Savior invites and whether He turns anyone away.
The other half reads it and reports whom the Lord says He created, remembers and brings His word to.
Read together after the first two; look for what the Savior asks of all those He came to save.

aligned_quotes.speaker: President Spencer W. Kimball
aligned_quotes.text: Teachableness [is] an ability to realize that all virtues and abilities are not concentrated in one’s self.

aligned_quotes.speaker: Elder Lebethoa
aligned_quotes.text: Whatever concerns, challenges, and struggles we may have in our lives, the answer is always Jesus Christ.

invitations.text: I urge you to keep the commandments and be true to the covenants so many of you have made to guide you along the covenant path.

Protect yourself with the weekly renewing of your covenants by partaking of the sacrament and with consistent efforts to live according to those sacred covenants. Those who have been endowed should include regular attendance at the temple. These simple practices will protect and strengthen you.
These promises from the Book of Mormon are true. Millions believe them and have had experiences to affirm their truth. I invite all to believe them.
I call upon all to act on these truths and to share them with others that we may all draw closer to Jesus Christ, our Savior.

takeaways: Whatever my concern or doubt, the way to overcome it is to get closer to Jesus Christ.
I can hold on to the first article of faith and wait upon the Lord while other things are uncertain.
The Savior invites all, and His grace is for all, including me and those I worry about.
act: Each day this week, take one step with prayer and scripture study aimed at the concern you wrote down.
Prepare for the sacrament on Sunday by thinking about one covenant you want to live more consistently.
If you have been endowed, set a date to attend the temple.
Share one Book of Mormon promise from 2 Nephi 26:33 with someone who may feel left out.
adapt: At home or with two or three people: skip the groups. Read the two paragraphs aloud together and build one list.
Large class: have groups write their lists on paper and call on three groups only.
Short on time: keep the first two segments and the last one, and read 2 Nephi 26:33 in place of the fifth segment.

youth.title: What to Do with a Question
youth.big_idea: Whatever questions or doubts we have, the way to overcome them is to get closer to Jesus Christ, hold on to what we know and keep learning.
youth.objective: Youth will be able to explain, in President Oaks's words, what to do when they or a friend have a question or doubt, and will choose one daily step to draw closer to Jesus Christ.
prepare: Read President Oaks's talk, The Gospel of Jesus Christ Is for All.
Bring small slips of paper, pens and a cup or bag to collect the slips.
Ask youth to bring phones with Gospel Library, or scriptures. Have the talk open on your own device.
Draw two columns on the board with the headings: Scientific method and Spiritual method.

segments.name: Fast start: the question slip
steps: As youth walk in, hand each a slip of paper. Ask them to write, without their name, one question someone their age might have about God, the Church or life. Collect the slips in a cup.
Pray. Then read two or three slips aloud without comment, choosing ones that will not point to any person.
Say honestly: we will not answer every one of these today. President Oaks, the President of the Church, taught us what to do while we have them.

segments.name: Find it: what did the prophet say?
steps: Form teams of two or three. Have them open the talk in Gospel Library and find the paragraphs that begin “We all have present or future concerns” and “We are all a work in progress.”
Give three minutes. Each team lists every action President Oaks gives for overcoming a concern or doubt. An item only counts if the team can point to the sentence.
Teams take turns naming one item until they run out. The last team with a new item wins.
Read the first key quote (T27.05) together and ask the question below.
questions: He said strong faith takes more than strong desire: it means “daily trying, one step at a time.” What is the difference between wanting faith and trying daily?

segments.name: Two ways to learn
steps: Point to the two columns. Explain that President Oaks said we are grateful for two methods of gaining knowledge. One is the scientific method and digital information, which he described as evolving and which may be inaccurate. The other is the spiritual method, which begins with faith in God and relies on scriptures, inspired teaching and personal revelation.
Ask youth to call out things they have learned by each method and write them in the columns.
Read the third key quote (T27.08). Ask a youth to restate it in their own words.

Read his direct instruction: “Never let your secular learning limit your spiritual horizons.” Discuss the questions below. Do not let this turn into a debate about any one scientific topic; the point is what he taught about how we learn.
questions: President Oaks said God knows all truth and expects us to learn by both methods. How does that change the way you treat something you cannot yet fit together?
He said resolving this kind of conflict can be a lengthy process. What helps you keep going when an answer is slow?

segments.name: Hold on
steps: Challenge the class to recite Articles of Faith 1:1 together from memory. Help them if they stall.
Read the second key quote (T27.06). Point out that this is a direct instruction from the prophet about what to hold on to when something else is uncertain.
Give one minute of silent writing on paper or a phone: three things I do know or believe about Heavenly Father, Jesus Christ and the Holy Ghost.
Read Sister Runia's words from the aligned quotes. Invite one or two youth to share one thing from their list.

segments.name: For all means all
steps: Read 2 Nephi 26:33 aloud, one phrase per person around the room. Ask youth to count how many kinds of people are named.
Read the fourth key quote (T27.07). Tell them President Oaks said this to members whose faith in Jesus Christ is diminishing.
Read Elder Renlund's words from the aligned quotes.
Read 2 Nephi 26:13. President Oaks taught that God's children in every nation have this promise: He “manifesteth himself unto all those who believe in him, by the power of the Holy Ghost.”
questions: Who at school or in our ward might think the Savior's invitation is not for them? What would help them feel that it is?

segments.name: Text back
steps: Describe a made-up situation: late at night a friend messages you to say that something they saw online does not fit with what they have learned at church, and now they are not sure what they believe.
In pairs, youth have two minutes to write a real reply of three sentences or fewer, using at least one thing President Oaks taught. It must sound like them, not like a talk.
Have two or three pairs read their replies. As a check for understanding, ask the class which teaching from President Oaks each reply used.

segments.name: One step this week
steps: Read the invitations. Note that President Oaks called upon all to act on these truths and to share them with others so that we may all draw closer to Jesus Christ.
Read his counsel about the sacrament (T27.10) and his promise that these simple practices will protect and strengthen us.
Each youth chooses one item from the act list and sets a daily reminder on their phone, or writes it on the back of a blank slip to keep.
Tell them that next week you will start by asking: what was your one step, and what did you notice? Bear a brief testimony of the Savior.

key_quotes.text: We all have present or future concerns or struggles we are trying to overcome. Those may include questions or doubts. Whatever they are, the way to overcome them is to get closer to our Savior, Jesus Christ.
Hold on to the first article of faith even if something else is uncertain. And while you wait, wait upon the Lord, which includes trusting in His timing as well as in His promises.
There is no ultimate conflict between knowledge obtained by these different methods because God, our omnipotent Eternal Father, knows all truth and expects us to learn by both methods.
We love you, young and old, men and women. So does the Lord God! He is relentless in His loving pursuit of each of you.

scriptures.use: Recite together from memory, then write three things you know or believe about the Godhead.
Read one phrase per person; count how many kinds of people the Savior invites to come unto Him.
Read after 2 Nephi 26:33; look for how the Savior promises to show Himself to those who believe in Him.

aligned_quotes.speaker: Sister Runia
aligned_quotes.text: Not understanding is not the same as not believing.

aligned_quotes.speaker: Elder Renlund
aligned_quotes.text: there is no asterisk excluding you from God’s richest blessings

invitations.text: Focus on developing your faith in God and the mission of His Son, Jesus Christ.
Hold on to the first article of faith even if something else is uncertain. And while you wait, wait upon the Lord
Never let your secular learning limit your spiritual horizons.
Protect yourself with the weekly renewing of your covenants by partaking of the sacrament and with consistent efforts to live according to those sacred covenants.
I call upon all to act on these truths and to share them with others that we may all draw closer to Jesus Christ, our Savior.

takeaways: Whatever my question or doubt, the way to overcome it is to get closer to Jesus Christ.
I can hold on to the first article of faith while I wait for other answers.
God knows all truth and expects me to learn by both the scientific method and the spiritual method.
act: For seven days, pray and read at least one verse of the Book of Mormon before opening any other app.
Memorize Articles of Faith 1:1 and say it to yourself when something feels uncertain.
On Sunday, take the sacrament with one covenant in mind that you want to live better this week.
Send one friend a verse or a line from President Oaks's talk that helped you.
adapt: At home with one or two youth: skip the teams and build the list together, then write the reply message side by side.
No phones: read the first two key quotes aloud twice and let teams list actions from listening.
Short on time: do the question slip, the find-it race, Hold on, and One step this week.

children.title: Jesus Invites Everyone
children.big_idea: Jesus Christ loves all people everywhere and invites everyone to come to Him.
children.objective: Children will be able to say that Jesus loves and invites everyone, and will name one way they can come closer to Him this week.
prepare: Read President Oaks's talk, especially where he teaches that the Lord loves all people and reaches out to all, everywhere.
Bring a picture of the Savior, a copy of the Book of Mormon and the Bible, a soft ball, paper and crayons.
Clear a space so children can walk across the room safely.

segments.name: Welcome and song
steps: Invite a child to pray. Sing Jesus Said Love Everyone.
Show the picture of the Savior. Tell the children that President Oaks, our prophet, taught that the Lord loves all people everywhere.
Say together twice, slowly, with arms open wide: Jesus loves everyone. Everyone can come to Him.

segments.name: Come over game
steps: Stand at one side of the room holding the picture of the Savior. The children stand at the other side.

Call groups to walk over a few at a time: everyone wearing something blue, everyone who likes to jump, everyone who has ever felt sleepy. Use only fun things like clothing colors and favorite activities.
Last, call: everyone who is a child of God. Wait until every child has come.
Explain: Jesus does not invite only some people. He invites all of us. Say the truth together again with arms open wide.
questions: How did it feel to wait for your turn to be called?
How does it feel to know Jesus invites everyone?

segments.name: What the Book of Mormon says
steps: Hold up the Book of Mormon. Tell the children President Oaks said it is a great witness that the Lord loves all people.
Read from 2 Nephi 26:33 the words President Oaks shared: the Savior invites “all to come unto him” and “he denieth none that come unto him.”
Explain that this means He does not turn anyone away. Have the children show it with their bodies: arms folded tight for turning someone away, then arms open wide for the way Jesus welcomes.
Read the phrase once more and let the children open their arms each time they hear the word all.
questions: Who does Jesus invite to come to Him?

segments.name: The Shepherd visits His sheep
steps: Tell the children that in the scriptures Jesus calls the people who follow Him His sheep. Read John 10:16 aloud.
Divide the children into three groups of sheep in three corners of the room. Name the corners: the land of Jerusalem, the Nephites, and others who had not yet heard His voice.

Carry the picture of the Savior to the first corner and tell, in simple words, that Jesus taught the people in the land of Jerusalem. Walk to the second corner: the Book of Mormon tells how He came and taught the Nephites. Walk to the third: He said He would visit others too.
At each corner, the sheep there say together: Jesus remembers us.
Gather all the children in the middle. Say: Jesus did not forget anyone. He reaches out to all.
questions: How do you think the people felt when Jesus came to them?

segments.name: All around the world ball
steps: Sit in a circle. Hold up the ball and say it is like the earth. President Oaks read a scripture where the Lord says He created all people and brings His word to all the nations of the earth.
Roll the ball to a child. The child names a place, near or far, and everyone says: Jesus loves the people there.
Keep rolling until each child has had a turn.

segments.name: One step at a time
steps: Place the picture of the Savior at one side of the room and line the children up at the other side.
Explain that President Oaks said faith means “daily trying, one step at a time,” with prayer and learning from the scriptures.

Ask the children to name ways to come closer to Jesus. For each one, everyone takes one step toward the picture. Help them think of: pray, read or listen to the scriptures, take the sacrament reverently, keep the commandments, tell someone about Jesus.
When all arrive, ask each child to tell you one step they liked best. This is your check that they understood.
questions: Which step can you take today?

segments.name: Draw and share
steps: Give each child paper and crayons. Ask them to draw themselves taking one step toward Jesus this week, such as praying or listening to a scripture story.
While they draw, tell them President Oaks asked all of us to share these truths with others so that we can all come closer to Jesus Christ.
Invite the children to show their drawing to someone they love and tell them: Jesus loves everyone.
Tell them that next week you will ask who they showed it to and what step they took. Bear your testimony that Jesus loves each of them, and close with prayer.

key_quotes.text: The Book of Mormon is a great witness that the Lord loves all people and reaches out to all, everywhere.
It means daily trying, one step at a time, with prayer and scriptural learning.

scriptures.use: Read only the phrases President Oaks quoted about the Savior inviting all; children open their arms each time they hear the word all.
Read aloud before the shepherd activity; ask the children to listen for the word sheep.
Older children read it aloud at the third corner to hear the Savior say He has other sheep to visit.

aligned_quotes.speaker: Elder Fale
aligned_quotes.text: I am a child of God and He loves me.

invitations.text: I call upon all to act on these truths and to share them with others that we may all draw closer to Jesus Christ, our Savior.

takeaways: Jesus invites me to come to Him and He will not turn me away.
I can come closer to Jesus one step at a time.
act: Say a prayer each morning and night this week.
Listen to or read one Book of Mormon story about Jesus.
Show your drawing to someone you love and tell them Jesus loves everyone.

adapt.younger: Ages 3–7: keep each part short and repeat the truth with open arms after every activity. Use two corners instead of three in the shepherd activity and walk with the children. In the ball circle, let a helper whisper a place name to a child who is unsure. After the come over game, have the children repeat after you Elder Fale's words from this conference: I am a child of God and He loves me.
adapt.older: Ages 8–11: ask an older child to read John 10:16 and another to read 3 Nephi 16:1 aloud, and let one lead the come over game by choosing the fun categories. Ask a harder question: President Oaks said faith takes daily trying. Why do you think coming to Jesus takes a step every day and not just one big step? Invite them to write their step under their drawing.
